visualCapture.title: Optional screen recording
visualCapture.body: With your consent, still images of your shared screen are sampled during the interview — no camera, no audio. Klymeo uses them to assess where the product flowed smoothly and where it stalled, in order to improve it. The still images are transmitted to Klymeo and analyzed automatically by an AI model; the result is seen by the provider conducting the study (researcher or organization). The still images themselves are discarded after the analysis — only the text notes derived from them remain. Taking part is voluntary: the interview continues normally without recording, and you can withdraw your consent at any time by ending the screen share.
visualCapture.truncated: Limit reached: only the first part will be analyzed.

eventConsent.title: Record interaction signals?
eventConsent.body: With your consent, Klymeo measures how you move during the conversation — clicks, scrolling and time per task — to understand where the product flowed smoothly and where it stalled. No camera, no audio, no emotion analysis; your typed text is not stored for this. Taking part is voluntary — the conversation continues normally without recording.

The participant is asked for consent at the start of the interview, before they can answer. Default: off.
plans.fldEventTracking: Interaction signals – clicks & time on task
plans.eventTrackingHint: When enabled, Klymeo measures non-biometric interaction behaviour during the interview — clicks, scrolling and time per task — to surface where it flowed and where it stalled. No audio, video or emotion analysis; raw input text is never stored. The participant is asked for consent at the start. Default: off.
plans.eventTrackingVoiceWarning: Heads up: interaction signals (clicks, scrolling, task success) are only captured in text interviews. This interview runs as voice — it won't produce any, and the usability summary will stay empty. Switch to a text interview to measure clicks and success.
plans.signalsHint: When enabled, Klymeo automatically annotates each completed interview with how answers were worded (e.g. enthusiastic, hesitant) and whether questions were answered directly — based solely on the text of the answers, never on the voice. The annotation is a hint with a verbatim quote, not a judgment about the person, visible to your team only, and runs only for sessions with documented participant consent. Default: off.

plans.interactionModeHint: This choice determines how participants experience the interview — and will become pricing-relevant: voice interviews will be priced separately. Default: text.
plans.interviewLengthHint: How deeply the AI interviewer probes per topic (Shallow/Medium/Deep = 1/2/4 follow-up layers). The total number of questions follows from depth × topics — an upper bound, never a quota: the interview ends earlier once a topic is exhausted. Studies with a stimulus set size their length automatically from the number of stimuli.
plans.lengthShortDesc: 1 question per topic — brief and focused.
plans.lengthStandardDesc: 2 questions per topic — recommended for most studies.
plans.lengthDeepDesc: Up to 4 questions per topic — digs deeper when there is substance.
plans.lengthAdvancedSummary: Advanced: set an exact question ceiling
plans.lengthCustomHint: Optional expert override of the depth automation: sets an exact question ceiling (wins over the chosen depth). Leave empty = depth controls the length.
plans.lengthLiveEstimate: Now: ≈ {questions} questions · ~{minutes} min — ends earlier on saturation
plans.lengthLiveEstimateCapped: Now: ≈ {questions} questions · ~{minutes} min — capped by the time limit
plans.errMaxRounds: Max. questions must be a whole number between 2 and 15.
plans.timeLimitHint: Optional time limit. Voice interviews end automatically once it elapses; text interviews show a visible countdown and close on the next answer after it passes. Empty = no limit.
plans.errMaxDuration: Time limit must be a whole number between 3 and 60 minutes.
plans.modeTextDesc: The AI interviewer asks its questions in a chat; participants answer by keyboard. Optionally an AI voice reads the questions aloud (read-aloud option below).
plans.modeVoiceDesc: An AI voice conducts the interview in real time — participants talk to the AI instead of typing. A text fallback stays available to participants; the AI disclosure is shown upfront.
plans.modeVoiceUnavailable: Voice interviews are not configured in this environment — please contact your administrator.
plans.marketGoalHeadline: What do you want to find out?
plans.ucSelectorTitle: What do you want to test?
plans.ucSelectorDesc: Pick a template — mode, opening questions and sample size are prefilled and stay editable.
plans.methodNoteGeneral: Klymeo asks about concrete past situations and workarounds instead of hypotheticals. Compliments don't count as signal — it keeps probing until there is a specific example.
plans.methodNoteBrand: Klymeo explores associations, images and feelings about the brand and deliberately stays broad rather than deep, so it doesn't overwrite the spontaneous perception.
plans.methodNoteCreative: Klymeo captures the first impression and the emotional effect — what stands out first and sticks, without overanalyzing.
plans.methodNoteConcept: Klymeo first checks whether the concept is understood, then how relevant it is — restrained on 'would you buy this', focused on genuine understanding.
plans.methodNoteUsability: Klymeo guides the person through a concrete task and probes hesitations, detours and misunderstandings — observable friction in their own words, no emotion scoring. Note: in this phase the task is a guide for the interview; click or screen recording comes later.
plans.ucGsT1Intent: What does a typical workday look like for you?
plans.ucGsT2Intent: Which tasks cost you the most time?
plans.ucGsT3Intent: What would you change about your tools?
plans.ucBrT1Intent: What's the first thing that comes to mind with [brand]?
plans.ucBrT3Intent: What does [brand] stand for — and what not?
plans.ucCrT2Intent: What message do you take away?
plans.ucCrT3Intent: What sticks with you the most?
plans.ucCoT1Intent: Describe the concept in your own words.
plans.ucCoT2Intent: What do you like, and what less so?
plans.ucCoT3Intent: Which variant appeals to you most, and why?
plans.ucUtT1Intent: How would you go about completing the task?
plans.ucUtT2Intent: Where were you unsure or couldn't find something?
plans.ucUtT3Intent: What would you have expected at that point?
plans.taskSectionDesc: The task the participant works on in the prototype or page. Klymeo runs the interview around this task — in this phase without click or screen recording.
plans.phTaskInstruction: e.g. In the prototype, find where you can cancel your subscription.
plans.taskSuccessHint: How do we know the task was completed? Optional — otherwise purely observational.
plans.taskUrlHint: Publicly reachable http(s) link to the prototype or page where the task is performed.
plans.errTaskInstruction: Please provide a task instruction for the usability test.
plans.ttsHint: When enabled, an AI voice reads the interviewer's questions aloud in the text interview — including the opening question. Participants can mute the sound themselves at any time. In voice-agent mode the AI speaks anyway, so this option doesn't apply there. Default: off.
plans.topicsFormDesc: The agent formulates questions on-the-fly from these topics — not a fixed question list. Each topic gets 2–4 turns in the conversation. Hypotheses are private steering, never read out loud.
plans.submitHelpNew: New plans start as drafts — you can edit topics, activate, and add participants on the next screen.
plans.submitHelpEdit: Saving overwrites the generator-created draft with your edits.

missionControl.pageIntro: Ask Konsoul across ALL of your organization's studies — the agent researches cross-study, loads the relevant studies on demand, counts exactly, and anchors every statement with a per-study citation.
missionControl.title: Ask across studies
missionControl.subtitle: Ask across all of your organization's study syntheses. Every statement is anchored to a verbatim quote from the study it cites — when there's no evidence you get an honest refusal instead of a fabricated answer.
missionControl.notReady: Once at least one study has been synthesized, you can ask across studies here.
missionControl.placeholder: e.g. "Which themes appear across studies?" or "Compare the findings from study A and B."
missionControl.anchoredHint: Every answer is anchored exclusively in the study syntheses — unsupported claims are dropped.
missionControl.errNoAccess: No access — please sign in and select an organization.

crossStudyAgent.title: Cross-Study agent
crossStudyAgent.subtitle: The agent researches across studies — it loads the relevant studies on demand, counts themes exactly, and compares. Every statement is anchored to a verbatim quote per study; anything it can't ground it labels as interpretation or honestly declines.
crossStudyAgent.notReady: Once at least one study has been synthesized, the agent can research here.
crossStudyAgent.placeholder: e.g. "In how many studies does the onboarding theme appear?" or "Compare the pricing findings across studies."
crossStudyAgent.anchoredHint: Grounded statements are anchored per study; numbers come from exact counting. Anything not grounded appears separately as interpretation.

syntheticTest.pageSubtitle: Let the interview bot run a few synthetic participants before real people start — to check the interview guide.
syntheticTest.disclaimerTitle: Only a test of the interview guide — not real market opinion
syntheticTest.disclaimerBody: Synthetic participants are AI personas, not real people. They show ONLY how the question bot behaves in a real conversation (does it hang? are the questions clear? does screening work? does a usable synthesis come out?). An AI persona is NOT real market opinion — do NOT base any business decisions on these answers. For real insight you need real participants.
syntheticTest.linkOutDesc: Try the interview guide with synthetic test participants before inviting real people.
syntheticTest.setupDesc: Pick the personas the interview bot should run through. Each selected persona becomes one synthetic participant.
syntheticTest.personasDesc: Default personas each test a different part of the guide. You can also describe your own personas in free text.

terse.label: Terse & busy
terse.blurb: Answers very briefly — tests whether the bot probes.

enthusiast.label: Enthusiastic
enthusiast.blurb: Talks a lot and digresses — tests whether the bot stays on plan.

skeptic.label: Skeptical
skeptic.blurb: Critical and guarded — tests handling of pushback.

price_conscious.label: Price-conscious
price_conscious.blurb: Steers to cost — tests handling of off-topic pricing.
